subject: history_social
notes: The Nilgiri Mountain Railway in Tamil Nadu, India, runs about 46 kilometers from Mettupalayam to the hill town of Udhagamandalam (Ooty).
Along the way it climbs from about 330 meters to about 2,200 meters above sea level.
Ordinary trains rely on friction between smooth wheels and smooth rails, which is not enough on very steep slopes.
On its steepest section, the railway uses a rack system: a toothed rail laid between the tracks, which a cogwheel under the locomotive grips to pull the train up.
The line was completed in 1908 and was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2005.
stem: The student wants to explain how the railway manages its steep climb. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Because ordinary trains cannot rely on wheel friction alone on steep slopes, the Nilgiri Mountain Railway uses a toothed rail between its tracks, gripped by a cogwheel under the locomotive, on its steepest section.
choices.B: The Nilgiri Mountain Railway climbs from about 330 meters to about 2,200 meters above sea level over a distance of about 46 kilometers.
choices.C: Completed in 1908, the Nilgiri Mountain Railway in Tamil Nadu, India, was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2005.
choices.D: On its steepest section, the Nilgiri Mountain Railway uses a rack system with a toothed rail laid between the tracks.

explanation.why: The goal asks how the climb is managed, so the key must describe the mechanism and show why it is needed. The third and fourth notes supply this: friction alone fails on steep slopes, so a cogwheel grips a toothed rail. Only one choice explains both the problem and the working of the solution.
explanation.A: Correct. It states why ordinary wheels are not enough and then explains how the toothed rail and cogwheel pull the train up.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This shows how steep the climb is but says nothing about how the train makes it.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This gives dates and recognition, not the method of climbing.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This names the rack system but does not say how it works or why it is needed, so it only half explains the climb.
